text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The Sofia Military Prosecution Office said it had cancelled an investigation against police officers suspected in using excessive force on January 10-11 when protesters clashed with riot police in front of Bulgaria's parliament, because there was no evidence of a crime.
Around 200 civilians were reported to have sought medical aid after the clashes.
-- Foreign investments in Bulgaria amounted to some $1 billion in the first seven months of this year, the Foreign Investment Agency said.

-- The parliamentary group of Bulgaria's oposition Socialist party said it would appeal to the Constitutional Court against the bill to open secret police files from the communist era passed by parliament last week because it violated civil rights of Bulgarians.

-- Ukraine's Ukrcomunbank is interested in buying a 25 percent stake in Bulgaria's private International Bank For Investments and Development (IBID), a IBID senior official said. IBID has been put in receiverchip by the central bank in April.
-- Bulgaria's northeast Black Sea port of Varna said it had posted 1.4 billion lev net profit for the first half of this year.
-- Bulgaria's Association of Tax Consultants said it would prepare by September a draft bill to cut Value Added Tax to 20 percent from 22 percent in a bid to boost the country's economic development.

-- Bulgaria's trade union Podkrepa said it expected pensions in the country to rise by 23 percent from October, bringing the minimum monthly pension to 33,210 levs. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 4145
